problems.name: Long-Video Evidence Sparsity and Efficient Selection
problems.evidence_sentence: Unlike conventional STVG methods that require the entire video sequence to make predictions at once, ART-STVG treats the video as streaming input and processes frames sequentially, enabling efficient handling of long videos.

problems.name: Spatio-Temporal and Object/Event-Level Grounding
problems.evidence_sentence: Furthermore, instead of parallel spatial and temporal localization, we propose a cascaded spatio-temporal design that connects the spatial decoder to the temporal decoder, allowing fine-grained spatial cues to assist complex temporal localization in long videos.

problems.name: Dataset, Benchmark, and Evaluation Mismatch
problems.evidence_sentence: However, existing research on spatio-temporal video grounding (STVG), given a textual query, mainly focuses on localizing targets in short videos of tens of seconds, typically less than one minute, which limits real-world applications.

methods.name: Object/Event/Spatio-Temporal Modules
methods.evidence_sentence: Towards Long-Form Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding In real scenarios, videos can span several minutes or even hours.

methods.name: Transformer/DETR-Style Proposal Decoding
methods.evidence_sentence: Furthermore, instead of parallel spatial and temporal localization, we propose a cascaded spatio-temporal design that connects the spatial decoder to the temporal decoder, allowing fine-grained spatial cues to assist complex temporal localization in long videos.

methods.name: Memory, Graph, or Structure Alignment
methods.evidence_sentence: To model spatio-temporal context, we design spatial and temporal memory banks and apply them to the decoders.

methods.name: Query-Conditioned Frame/Clip Selection
methods.evidence_sentence: Since memories from different moments are not always relevant to the current frame, we introduce simple yet effective memory selection strategies to provide more relevant information to the decoders, significantly improving performance.
